**Finding submitted: Compliant** — no redline, document text unchanged.

To be transparent: no substantive repair was available or appropriate here. The verifier's own narrative affirms every element of the finding — correct status, correct paragraphs, correct playbook position, and correctly no redline. The single "failed" line item (`general-solicitation carve-out present`) is the same non-probative heuristic the verifier itself dismissed in the following sentence. I re-validated the document once more across all detection phrasings before re-submitting, and confirmed the position is unchanged:

- **§ 14.8 Personnel** (p0182) — supervision/direction of each party's own personnel, IBM's assignment rights, IBM's use of Subcontractors and Affiliates. No hiring restriction.
- **§ 14.16 Freedom of Action** (p0200) — "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others." Runs in our favour.

**Why I did not act on the failed check:** the carve-out and duration heuristics measure attributes *of* a non-solicit clause. There is no such clause, so their failure signals absence, not a defect. Satisfying them literally would mean drafting a non-solicit onto Bluefly that IBM never requested, then carving it back — a strictly worse outcome than the preferred position we already hold. I have left the text untouched.

This sits at the **preferred** position, not the fallback. Further re-submission cycles on this rule will produce the same result unless new clause text surfaces.
